Introduction to LLMOpsLLMOps 导论

— 原书第 37 页 —

The size and complexity of LLMs' architecture can make productionizing these models incredibly hard. Productionizing means not just deploying a model but also monitoring it, evaluating it, and optimizing its performance.

LLM 架构的规模与复杂度，使得把这些模型推向生产环境异常艰难。所谓 productionizing（生产化），不只是部署模型，还包括监控、评估和性能优化。

There are constantly new challenges. Depending on your application, these may include how to process data, how to store and dynamically adapt prompts, how to monitor user interaction, and—most pressing—how to prevent the model from spreading misinformation or memorizing training data (which can lead it to release personal information). That's why operationalizing LLMs, which means managing them day-to-day in production, requires a new framework.

新挑战层出不穷。根据应用不同，可能包括：如何处理数据、如何存储并动态调整提示词、如何监控用户交互，以及最紧迫的——如何防止模型传播错误信息或记忆训练数据（这可能导致它泄露个人信息）。正因如此，把 LLM 运维起来（即在生产环境中日复一日地管理它们）需要一套新框架。

LLMOps, as it's called, is an operational framework for putting LLM applications in production. Although its name and principles are inspired by its older siblings, MLOps and DevOps, LLMOps is significantly more nuanced. The LLMOps framework can help companies reduce technical debt, maintain compliance, deal with LLMs' dynamic and experimental nature, and minimize operational and reputational risk by avoiding common pitfalls.

这就是 LLMOps——一套把 LLM 应用推向生产的运维框架。尽管它的名字和原则借鉴了兄长 MLOps 和 DevOps，但 LLMOps 要细致得多。LLMOps 框架能帮助企业减少技术债、维持合规、应对 LLM 动态且实验性的特质，并通过避开常见陷阱来最小化运营与声誉风险。

This chapter starts by discussing what LLMOps is and how and where it departs from MLOps. We'll then introduce you to the LLMOps engineer role and where it fits into existing ML teams. From there, we'll look at how to measure LLMOps readiness within teams, assess your organization's LLMOps maturity, and identify crucial KPIs for measuring success. Toward the end of this chapter, we will outline some challenges that are specific to productionizing LLM applications.

本章先讨论 LLMOps 是什么，它在哪些方面、如何与 MLOps 分道扬镳。随后介绍 LLMOps 工程师这一角色，以及它在现有 ML 团队中的位置。接着我们会看如何衡量团队的 LLMOps 准备度、评估组织的 LLMOps 成熟度，并识别衡量成功的关键 KPI。章末会概述一些 LLM 应用生产化特有的挑战。

— 原书第 38 页 —

What Are Operational Frameworks?什么是运维框架？

Operational frameworks provide a structured approach to managing complex workflows and pipelines within an organization. These frameworks integrate tools and practices to automate and streamline organizational processes and ensure consistency and quality across the project lifecycle.

运维框架为组织内复杂工作流和流水线的管理提供结构化方法。它们整合工具与实践，将组织流程自动化、精简化，并在整个项目生命周期内保证一致性与质量。

Some of the earliest operational frameworks can be traced back to military strategy and the Industrial Revolution. Two of the most popular ones, both introduced in 1986, are Toyota's Lean Production System, which put Toyota ahead of most of its contemporaries, and Six Sigma, Motorola's data-driven approach to improving processes and reducing defects.

最早的运维框架可追溯到军事战略和工业革命。1986 年问世、最流行的两个框架是丰田精益生产方式（让丰田领先于同时代多数企业）和六西格玛（摩托罗拉以数据驱动改进流程、减少缺陷的方法）。

In 2008, the tech industry began to adopt what is now one of the most popular operational frameworks in software: DevOps. (The term combines software development and operations.) In 2018, MLOps, an operational framework for non-generative machine learning (ML) models, became the talk of the town; since then we've seen SecOps (Security Operations), DataSecOps, and many more.

2008 年，科技行业开始采用如今软件领域最流行的运维框架之一：DevOps（这个词合并了软件开发与运维）。2018 年，面向非生成式机器学习（ML）模型的运维框架 MLOps 成为热门话题；此后又出现了 SecOps（安全运维）、DataSecOps 等众多变体。

With the massive adoption of LLMs in 2023, a new operational framework started floating around within companies that were building LLM applications: LLMOps. LLMOps is still in its infancy, but as generative models become integral to software products, its popularity is likely to boom.

随着 2023 年 LLM 的大规模采用，一种新的运维框架开始在构建 LLM 应用的公司中流传：LLMOps。LLMOps 仍处于初期，但随着生成式模型成为软件产品不可或缺的部分，它的流行度很可能爆发。

Figure 2-1 shows the slow rise of Ops frameworks over the years. Use of LLMOps started to pick up with the mass adoption of LLMs in early 2023. As of this writing, more and more enterprises are realizing that they can add value and profit with LLM-based offerings, leading to an upward trend for LLMOps. In fact, 2025 may be the best year yet for LLMOps frameworks.

图 2-1 展示了这些年 Ops 框架缓慢上升的曲线。LLMOps 的使用随着 2023 年初 LLM 的大规模采用开始抬头。截至本书写作时，越来越多企业意识到它们可以用基于 LLM 的产品增加价值和利润，推动 LLMOps 呈上升趋势。事实上，2025 年可能是 LLMOps 框架迄今最好的一年。

Deploying LLMs can be as simple as integrating a chatbot into your website via an API or as complicated as building your own LLM and frontend from scratch. But maintaining them to be performant (productionizing them)—that is, keeping them reliable, scalable, secure, and robust—is a massive challenge. This book, like LLMOps, is focused on exactly this question: what happens after you deploy your LLM in production?

部署 LLM 可以简单到通过 API 把聊天机器人集成进你的网站，也可以复杂到从零构建自己的 LLM 和前端。但要把它们维护得高性能（即生产化）——让它们可靠、可扩展、安全、健壮——才是巨大的挑战。本书和 LLMOps 一样，聚焦的正是这个问题：把 LLM 部署到生产环境之后会发生什么？

From MLOps to LLMOps: Why Do We Need a New Framework?从 MLOps 到 LLMOps：我们为何需要新框架？

There is some overlap between MLOps and LLMOps; both deal with the operational lifecycles of ML models, after all. They also share common principles in terms of managing ML workflows. However, the two frameworks diverge in their primary focuses and objectives. While MLOps handles non-generative models (both language and computer vision), LLMOps deals with generative language models—and thus with mammoth levels of complexity. The complexity of these models owes not only to their scale and architecture but also to the unique processes involved in data engineering, domain adaptation, evaluation, and monitoring for them. The key distinctions are apparent in LLMs' prediction transparency, latency, and memory and computational requirements.

MLOps 与 LLMOps 有重叠——毕竟二者都处理 ML 模型的运维生命周期，在管理 ML 工作流上也共享共同原则。但两者的主要关注点和目标分道扬镳。MLOps 处理非生成式模型（语言和计算机视觉都算），LLMOps 则处理生成式语言模型——因而面对的是庞然量级的复杂度。这些模型的复杂不仅来自规模和架构，还来自其数据工程、领域适配、评估和监控所涉及的独特流程。关键差异体现在 LLM 的预测透明度、延迟，以及内存和计算需求上。

— 原书第 40 页 —

Perhaps the biggest difference is the shift in how end users consume these models. Non-generative ML models are predictive tools used for passive consumption, such as in dashboarding, recommendations, and analytics. By contrast, LLM applications are deployed as Software 3.0 in consumer-facing applications for active user interaction. This brings several challenges from Software 1.0 (DevOps) back to the surface. In fact, it wouldn't be wrong to say that LLMOps shares more similarities with DevOps than with MLOps.

或许最大的差异在于终端用户消费这些模型方式的转变。非生成式 ML 模型是供被动消费的预测工具，用于仪表板、推荐、分析等。相比之下，LLM 应用作为 Software 3.0 部署在面向消费者的应用中，供用户主动交互。这把 Software 1.0（DevOps）时代的若干挑战又带回了台面。事实上，说 LLMOps 与 DevOps 的共同点多于与 MLOps 的共同点，并不为过。

Building your own generative AI application requires tools, frameworks, and expectations to match the scale and complexity of these models, and this is far beyond the scope of the existing MLOps solutions. To help you understand the differences between the various kinds of Ops frameworks, let's do a thought experiment.

构建自己的生成式 AI 应用所需的工具、框架和预期，必须匹配这些模型的规模与复杂度，这远远超出了现有 MLOps 方案的范围。为帮助你理解各类 Ops 框架之间的差异，我们来做个思想实验。

Imagine MLOps as being something like building a small home from the ground up. In comparison, DevOps, which deals with the entire product lifecycle, would be like developing a large shopping complex. And LLMOps? It's more like building the Burj Khalifa. For all three frameworks, you are working with the same construction materials: wood, steel, concrete, bricks, hammers, and so on. Much of the basic process is the same, too: you lay down the foundation, lay down the plumbing, and finally build the walls. But you wouldn't contract your local construction workers to engineer the Burj Khalifa, would you?

把 MLOps 想象成从零盖一座小住宅。相比之下，处理整个产品生命周期的 DevOps 就像开发一座大型购物中心。而 LLMOps？更像建造哈利法塔。三个框架用的建材都一样：木材、钢材、混凝土、砖、锤子等等。基本流程也大同小异：打地基、铺管线、最后砌墙。但你不会把哈利法塔的工程包给本地建筑工人，对吧？

Most of MLOps for natural language modeling is based on building smaller, discriminative models for tasks like sentiment analysis, topic modeling, and summarization. For these tasks, you first hypothesize ideal features, model your data as a function of those features, and then optimize the model for that specific task.

面向自然语言建模的 MLOps，大多是为情感分析、主题建模、摘要等任务构建较小的判别式模型。对这些任务，你先假设理想特征，把数据建模为这些特征的函数，再针对该特定任务优化模型。

LLMs, by contrast, are generative, domain agnostic, and task agnostic. That fundamental difference means you can use the same model for summarizing or for answering questions, without having to fine-tune it.

LLM 则相反：它是生成式的、领域无关、任务无关。这一根本差异意味着你可以用同一个模型做摘要或问答，而无需微调。

The best use cases for LLMs are when you don't know what features to optimize for (or, even better, if the features are too abstract) and when you need to model multimodal data within a single pipeline. Unlike smaller discriminative models, LLMs don't rely on predefined features or task-specific architectures. Instead, as you learned in Chapter 1, they are trained on vast amounts of text data to learn the patterns and structures in language itself. For LLMs, the training process involves a loss function, which measures how well the model's generated outputs match the expected outputs across various tasks. For example, during training, the model might generate a sequence of text; the loss function calculates the difference between this generated sequence and the target sequence.

LLM 最佳用例出现在你不知道该优化什么特征时（更好的情况是：特征过于抽象），以及你需要在单条流水线中建模多模态数据时。与较小的判别式模型不同，LLM 不依赖预定义特征或任务专用架构。相反，如第 1 章所述，它们在海量文本数据上训练，学习语言本身的模式与结构。对 LLM 而言，训练过程涉及损失函数，衡量模型在各任务上生成输出与期望输出的匹配程度。例如训练时模型可能生成一段文本序列；损失函数计算该生成序列与目标序列之间的差异。

Additionally, for a standard comparison, the hyperparameter space for a 175-billion-parameter GPT-4 model would likely be approximately 1,500 times larger than that for a standard discriminative BERT model (which has 110 million parameters). This

另外做个标准对比：一个 1750 亿参数的 GPT-4 模型，其超参数空间大约是标准判别式 BERT 模型（1.1 亿参数）的 1500 倍。这

Four Goals for LLMOpsLLMOps 的四大目标

LLMOps operates on an LLM-specific set of design pattern principles to ensure that your LLM applications achieve four key goals: security, scalability, robustness, and reliability. Let's take a closer look at these goals:

LLMOps 基于一套 LLM 专用的设计模式原则运行，确保你的 LLM 应用达成四大目标：安全、可扩展、鲁棒、可靠。我们逐一细看：

  • Security. Minimizing the regulatory, reputational, and operational risks associated with deploying LLM applications in production.安全（Security）。最小化与在生产环境部署 LLM 应用相关的监管、声誉和运营风险。
  • Scalability. Building, storing, and maintaining LLM applications that can generalize across data and scale efficiently on demand while optimizing latency, throughput, and costs.可扩展（Scalability）。构建、存储和维护 LLM 应用，使其能跨数据泛化、按需高效扩缩，同时优化延迟、吞吐和成本。
  • Robustness. Maintaining high performance of LLM applications over time in the face of data drift, model drift, third-party updates, and other challenges.鲁棒（Robustness）。面对数据漂移、模型漂移、第三方更新和其他挑战，长期维持 LLM 应用的高性能。
  • Reliability. Implementing rigorous inference monitoring, error handling, and redundancy mechanisms to prevent downtime and failures.可靠（Reliability）。实施严格的推理监控、错误处理和冗余机制，防止宕机和故障。

LLMOps teams automate repetitive processes to more quickly optimize these applications at scale and avoid those "LLM-oops!" moments. Another key aspect of the LLMOps framework is fostering consistency, transparency, and collaboration between diverse interdisciplinary teams. These teams often include data engineers, data scientists, research scientists, software engineers, and business operations teams.

LLMOps 团队把重复流程自动化，以便更快地大规模优化这些应用，避免那些“LLM 哎呀！”时刻。LLMOps 框架的另一关键方面，是促进多元跨学科团队之间的一致性、透明度和协作。这些团队通常包括数据工程师、数据科学家、研究科学家、软件工程师和业务运营团队。

LLMOps is an entirely new field, so, as of this writing in 2025, there are very few mature tools and resources available. The LLMOps teams at various organizations are thus developing their tools and processes internally, based on prototypical open source libraries and toolkits.

LLMOps 是一个全新领域，因此截至 2025 年写作时，成熟的工具和资源还很少。各组织的 LLMOps 团队于是基于原型开源库和工具包，在内部开发自己的工具和流程。

LLMOps Teams and RolesLLMOps 团队与角色

Today, there are two kinds of companies out there building with LLMs: the newer startups, which focus primarily on LLM applications, and companies with existing ML models that are now building their own GenAI teams.

如今，用 LLM 构建产品的公司分两类：一类是较新的初创公司，主要专注 LLM 应用；另一类是已有 ML 模型、现在正在组建自己 GenAI 团队的公司。

In the latter category, there are so few skilled Ops professionals that most companies recruit ML engineer candidates internally and then upskill them to LLMOps, instead of hiring externally. A major reason for this is a general lack of clarity around use cases as well as the expected job responsibilities. So the current norm is to hire 8 to 10 people internally from different departments, which could include product managers, full-stack engineers, system architects, data engineers, data scientists, ML engineers,

在后一类公司中，熟练的 Ops 专业人才极其稀缺，多数公司从内部招聘 ML 工程师候选人，再把他们提升为 LLMOps，而非外部招聘。一个主要原因是用例和岗位职责普遍不清晰。因此当前的常态是从不同部门内部招 8 到 10 人，可能包括产品经理、全栈工程师、系统架构师、数据工程师、数据科学家、ML 工程师、

— 原书第 43 页 —

platform engineers, cybersecurity professionals, and developer advocates. Many companies want someone who already understands the business inside and out to test the feasibility of several potential use cases and projects before committing to one.

平台工程师、网络安全专家和开发者布道师。许多公司希望找一个已经对业务了如指掌的人，在押注某一用例/项目之前，先测试若干潜在用例和项目的可行性。

Newer startups, however, have no choice but to build a team from the ground up. These teams can look very different, depending on whether they are working on LLMOps infrastructure (LLMOps SaaS companies) or LLM use cases such as copywriting, education, or process optimization. Figure 2-2 provides a very basic model of an LLMOps team, but these teams come in all shapes and sizes, with different levels of business and technical maturity. (Later in the chapter, we'll look at how to assess your company's LLMOps maturity.)

而较新的初创公司别无选择，只能从零组建团队。这些团队形态差异很大，取决于他们是做 LLMOps 基础设施（LLMOps SaaS 公司）还是做文案、教育、流程优化等 LLM 用例。图 2-2 给出了一个非常基础的 LLMOps 团队模型，但实际团队形状和规模各异，业务和技术成熟度也不同。（本章后文会讲如何评估你公司的 LLMOps 成熟度。）

Most companies cannot afford the cost of building and training an LLM for use in their application. Instead, most choose to use a foundational model. This is where AI engineers come in: to build a quick proof of concept using LLMOps tools. Most come from a software-engineering background; they may know how to build a full-stack application quickly, but don't necessarily have a deep understanding of ML/LLM models' inner workings or how to optimize them.

多数公司负担不起为自己的应用构建并训练 LLM 的成本。因此大多数选择使用基础模型。这时 AI 工程师登场：用 LLMOps 工具快速构建概念验证。他们大多有软件工程背景；可能知道如何快速搭建全栈应用，但未必深入理解 ML/LLM 模型的内部工作原理或优化方法。

— 原书第 44 页 —

Once the proof of concept is completed, building, deploying, and optimizing ML models for the business falls to LLM engineers, ML scientists (interchangeable titles, depending on the organization), and LLMOps engineers tasked as reliability engineers.

概念验证完成后，为业务构建、部署和优化 ML 模型的工作，就落到 LLM 工程师、ML 科学家（不同组织叫法互换）以及担任可靠性工程师的 LLMOps 工程师身上。

If a team chooses to deploy an LLM application using API integration, the initial deployment will be pretty straightforward. The LLMOps engineers work alongside AI engineers to scale the model and improve its performance. Ideally, each AI engineer is paired with an LLMOps engineer; the AI engineer can focus on adapting and fine-tuning the model to meet the business needs, while the LLMOps engineer manages deployment and optimization. For open source models, managing deployment automatically falls to the LLMOps engineer.

如果团队选择通过 API 集成部署 LLM 应用，初始部署会相当直接。LLMOps 工程师与 AI 工程师并肩扩缩模型、提升性能。理想情况下，每位 AI 工程师都配一位 LLMOps 工程师：AI 工程师专注适配和微调模型以满足业务需求，LLMOps 工程师管理部署和优化。对于开源模型，部署管理自然落到 LLMOps 工程师身上。

As the tech industry moves from non-generative models to generative models, it is shifting away from feature engineering, or creating features to model the data and experimenting with different hyperparameters to optimize performance. Generative models, and specifically LLMs, do not require feature engineering. Today, the core requirements are usually prompt engineering or building a RAG pipeline—skills that lie within the domain of AI engineers.

随着科技行业从非生成式模型转向生成式模型，它也在远离特征工程——即创建特征来建模数据、试验不同超参数以优化性能。生成式模型（尤其是 LLM）不需要特征工程。如今核心要求通常是提示工程或构建 RAG 流水线——这些技能属于 AI 工程师的领域。

Another big shift is that the data engineering pipeline and the monitoring and evaluation pipeline have become far more complex. Evaluating LLMs is much more than straightforward quantitative scoring. Some industry benchmarks exist—like BLEU, a benchmark used to evaluate machine translation, and ROUGE, a benchmark used to evaluate summarization, but these are only loosely correlated with application performance. Moving to a model that has a better score is no guarantee of better user satisfaction. Standardized scores may be good for comparing LLMs in general, but ultimately users care about whether the LLM application is solving their problem.

另一大转变是数据工程流水线和监控评估流水线都变得复杂得多。评估 LLM 远不止直白的定量打分。行业里有一些基准——例如用于机器翻译评估的 BLEU、用于摘要评估的 ROUGE——但它们与应用性能只有松散相关。换一个分数更高的模型，并不能保证用户满意度更高。标准化分数或许适合总体比较 LLM，但最终用户关心的是 LLM 应用有没有解决他们的问题。

In addition, since LLMs are deployed in consumer-facing applications, metrics like perceived latency and throughput become make-or-break factors in market competition. The model is not the only deciding factor: the deployment, evaluation, and monitoring pipelines are also at the front and center of performance assessment. Let's look at some of the roles involved in these pipelines:

此外，由于 LLM 部署在面向消费者的应用中，感知延迟和吞吐等指标成为市场竞争中的成败关键。模型并非唯一决定因素：部署、评估和监控流水线也处于性能评估的前沿和中心。我们来看看这些流水线涉及的一些角色：

Data engineer. Data engineers are professionals responsible for designing, building, and maintaining systems and pipelines that enable the efficient collection, storage, and transformation of data as well as access to it. Their work ensures that data is available, reliable, and organized in a way that allows data scientists and other engineers to create and evaluate models and data-driven applications. Data retrieval and movement are the most fundamental skills for data engineers, but as they progress in their career, developing data architectures becomes more important.

数据工程师。数据工程师负责设计、构建和维护系统与流水线，使数据能被高效采集、存储、转换和访问。他们的工作确保数据可用、可靠、有条理，让数据科学家和其他工程师能创建并评估模型和数据驱动应用。数据检索和搬运是数据工程师最基本的技能，但随着职业发展，数据架构设计变得更重要。

— 原书第 45 页 —

Data engineering for LLMs requires specialized understanding: how to chunk the data, what tokenization model to use, and so on. Thus, it's best to pair each data engineer with an ML scientist (with an LLM engineering background) along with the LLMOps engineer for automating and streamlining LLM systems at scale.

面向 LLM 的数据工程需要专业理解：如何切分数据、用什么分词模型等等。因此最好给每位数据工程师配一位 ML 科学家（有 LLM 工程背景）和一位 LLMOps 工程师，以便大规模自动化和精简 LLM 系统。

AI engineer. The core skill set of an AI engineer is full-stack engineering and development (React, Node.js, Django) plus familiarity with the common LLMOps tools and frameworks for deploying applications, like LangChain and LlamaIndex. They need a foundational understanding of end-to-end AI application development, including prompt engineering and RAG systems. Companies building their teams from scratch usually look to hire AI engineers who also know a lot about using cloud services to deploy and manage AI applications and have experience working with external APIs and vector databases.

AI 工程师。AI 工程师的核心技能是全栈工程与开发（React、Node.js、Django），外加熟悉 LangChain、LlamaIndex 等部署应用常用的 LLMOps 工具和框架。他们需要端到端 AI 应用开发的基础理解，包括提示工程和 RAG 系统。从零组建团队的公司，通常想招既懂云服务部署和管理 AI 应用、又有外部 API 和向量数据库经验的 AI 工程师。

ML scientist. The day-to-day work of an ML scientist, NLP scientist, or LLM engineer involves researching, designing, and optimizing LLMs using frameworks like PyTorch, TensorFlow, and JAX. This role requires a deep understanding of NLP algorithms and tasks, such as tokenization, named-entity recognition (NER), sentiment analysis, and machine translation. Candidates should know model architectures and training and fine-tuning processes.

ML 科学家。ML 科学家、NLP 科学家或 LLM 工程师的日常工作，是用 PyTorch、TensorFlow、JAX 等框架研究、设计和优化 LLM。该角色需要深入理解 NLP 算法和任务，如分词、命名实体识别（NER）、情感分析、机器翻译。候选人应了解模型架构以及训练和微调流程。

LLMOps engineer. The goal of an LLMOps engineer is to ensure that LLM applications remain reliable, robust, secure, and scalable. The day-to-day work involves building and maintaining operational LLM pipelines as a project owner.

LLMOps 工程师。LLMOps 工程师的目标是确保 LLM 应用始终可靠、鲁棒、安全、可扩展。日常工作是以项目负责人身份构建和运维 LLM 流水线。

Let's now look at the LLMOps engineer role in more detail.

现在我们来更详细地看看 LLMOps 工程师这一角色。

The LLMOps Engineer RoleLLMOps 工程师角色

This role requires extensive expertise in deploying, monitoring, fine-tuning, training, scaling, and optimizing LLM models in production environments; infrastructure and platform engineering; data engineering; and system reliability.

该角色需要在以下方面具备广博专长：生产环境中 LLM 模型的部署、监控、微调、训练、扩缩和优化；基础设施与平台工程；数据工程；以及系统可靠性。

Companies building LLM teams usually seek LLMOps engineers who understand the unique challenges associated with LLMs and are experienced in making build-versus-buy trade-off, including by weighing cost efficiency against system performance.

组建 LLM 团队的公司通常寻找这样的 LLMOps 工程师：理解 LLM 相关的独特挑战，并有做出“自建 vs 采购”权衡的经验，包括在成本效率与系统性能之间权衡。

To stand out as a candidate for this role, you'll need proficiency in a unique blend of specialized skills and a deep technical understanding of the entire LLM lifecycle, from data management to model deployment and monitoring. You'll also need to be a problem solver, a strong team player, and an effective communicator as well as meticulously detail oriented.

要在这个角色的候选人中脱颖而出，你需要熟练掌握一套独特的专业技能组合，并对从数据管理到模型部署与监控的整个 LLM 生命周期有深入技术理解。你还需要是问题解决者、优秀的团队协作者、高效的沟通者，并且极度注重细节。

There are two ways to fill an LLMOps engineer role: you can hire externally, or you can hire internally and upskill your people, training ML engineers to become LLMOps engineers. This section will look at external hiring first and then discuss how to upskill current employees.

填补 LLMOps 工程师岗位有两种方式：外部招聘，或内部招聘并提升现有人员——培训 ML 工程师成为 LLMOps 工程师。本节先看外部招聘，再讨论如何提升现有员工。

If you're hiring for this role, other skills to look for in candidates for LLMOps engineering roles include experience or proficiency in:

  • Understanding ML metrics like accuracy, precision, recall, and PR-AUC理解准确率、精确率、召回率、PR-AUC 等 ML 指标

  • Building Ops pipelines for data engineering, deployment, and infrastructure as code (IaC) using tools like Terraform, managing vector databases, and ETL processes for large-scale training datasets用 Terraform 等工具构建数据工程、部署和基础设施即代码（IaC）的 Ops 流水线，管理向量数据库，以及大规模训练数据集的 ETL 流程

Hiring Internally: Upskilling an MLOps Engineer into an LLMOps Engineer内部招聘：把 MLOps 工程师提升为 LLMOps 工程师

The gap between MLOps engineers and LLMOps engineers is significant in terms of the scale, complexity, and the technical challenges involved in their roles. Thus, upskilling an existing employee requires a focused effort to build their understanding.

MLOps 工程师与 LLMOps 工程师之间，在角色涉及的规模、复杂度和技术挑战上差距显著。因此，提升现有员工需要专注投入以构建他们的理解。

That said, the foundational skills of MLOps—such as model deployment, automation, and cloud management—provide a solid base from which to grow. With dedicated learning and hands-on experience, an MLOps engineer can transition into the LLMOps domain effectively. The core upside of hiring internally is that candidates are already aligned with the organization's values and culture and have a keen understanding of its KPIs.

话虽如此，MLOps 的基础技能——如模型部署、自动化和云管理——提供了可成长的坚实基础。通过专门学习和动手实践，MLOps 工程师可以有效转型到 LLMOps 领域。内部招聘的核心好处是：候选人已经与组织价值观和文化对齐，并且对其 KPI 有敏锐理解。

To excel, new LLMOps engineers need resources and training to deepen their understanding of large-scale model architectures and transformer architectures, attention mechanisms, infrastructure management, and LLM-specific optimization techniques. They also need to understand how LLMs differ from non-generative ML models. We recommend pairing them up with LLM engineers to experiment with and evaluate different models.

要胜任，新晋 LLMOps 工程师需要资源和培训来加深对大规模模型架构、Transformer 架构、注意力机制、基础设施管理和 LLM 专用优化技术的理解。他们还需要理解 LLM 与非生成式 ML 模型的差异。我们建议让他们与 LLM 工程师结对，试验并评估不同模型。

This role isn't just about building an app that uses LLMs. LLMOps engineers also manage the balance among cost, cloud resources, and user experience and handle huge unstructured datasets. Therefore, pair them with data engineers to help build a data-processing pipeline so they can familiarize themselves with the data sources at their disposal, how the data is structured in the databases, how different databases retrieve information, what the company's latency expectations are, and how to handle data filtering. Allow them to introduce multi-node setups and distributed systems for different models while focusing on cost optimization and errors. Get them to benchmark different LLM models and debug their performance optimization. Finally, allow them to present their logging practices and the guardrails they have set up for maintaining reliability and performance at scale.

这个角色不只是构建一个使用 LLM 的应用。LLMOps 工程师还要管理成本、云资源和用户体验之间的平衡，并处理海量非结构化数据集。因此让他们与数据工程师结对，帮助搭建数据处理流水线，从而熟悉可用的数据源、数据在数据库中如何组织、不同数据库如何检索信息、公司的延迟预期是什么、以及如何处理数据过滤。允许他们为不同模型引入多节点设置和分布式系统，同时关注成本优化和错误。让他们基准测试不同 LLM 模型并调试性能优化。最后，让他们展示自己的日志实践，以及为大规模维持可靠性和性能所设的护栏。

Most MLOps engineers already have skills in model versioning, data versioning, managing rollbacks, and GitHub actions, so upskilling these professionals can be an effective strategy for building a strong LLMOps team.

多数 MLOps 工程师已具备模型版本管理、数据版本管理、回滚管理和 GitHub Actions 等技能，因此提升这些专业人员是组建强大 LLMOps 团队的有效策略。

— 原书第 51 页 —

Next, let's look at how to make sure the goals of your LLMOps engineers are aligned with your organizational goals.

接下来，我们看看如何确保 LLMOps 工程师的目标与组织目标对齐。

LLMs and Your OrganizationLLM 与你的组织

You learned at the beginning of this chapter that the four key goals of the LLMOps framework are security, scalability, robustness, and reliability. For LLMOps teams, then, the next big question is how to measure the application's performance against those goals. How will you know you're succeeding? The company's expectations should be clearly defined and remain quantitatively, as well as qualitatively, measurable at all times.

你在章首已知 LLMOps 框架的四大关键目标是安全、可扩展、鲁棒、可靠。对 LLMOps 团队来说，下一个大问题就是如何对照这些目标衡量应用的性能。你怎么知道自己成功了？公司的期望应当被清晰定义，并始终保持可量化、可定性衡量。

Three kinds of metrics will allow you to measure your team's performance toward its goals: SLOs, SLAs, and KPIs. These terms are in common usage among site reliability engineers, and now LLMOps teams are rapidly adopting them as well:

有三类指标可让你衡量团队朝目标迈进的表现：SLO、SLA 和 KPI。这些术语在站点可靠性工程师中常用，如今 LLMOps 团队也在快速采用：

  • Service-level objectives (SLOs). Service-level objectives are specific, measurable targets set by an organization to gauge the quality of its services internally. They define what level of service the organization aims to achieve. For example, an SLO for a cloud-hosting company might be to ensure that server uptime is at least 99.9% per month.服务水平目标（SLO）。SLO 是组织为内部衡量服务质量而设定的具体、可度量的目标，定义组织希望达成的服务水平。例如，云托管公司的 SLO 可能是确保每月服务器正常运行时间至少 99.9%。
  • Service-level agreements (SLAs). Service-level agreements are formal contracts between a service provider and a customer that define the level of service the provider commits to deliver. They typically include specific performance goals and stipulate remedies if those metrics are not met. For example, if the uptime for an internet provider falls below 99.9% annually, the SLA might stipulate that the customer will receive a 10% discount on its next billing cycle.服务水平协议（SLA）。SLA 是服务提供商与客户之间的正式合同，定义提供商承诺交付的服务水平。通常包含具体性能目标，并规定未达标时的补救措施。例如，如果某互联网提供商年正常运行时间低于 99.9%，SLA 可能规定客户在下一账单周期获得 10% 折扣。
  • Key performance indicators (KPIs). Key performance indicators measure the overall success and performance of specific business activities. They provide insight into how well the organization is achieving its strategic objectives. For example, an important KPI for an app might be its churn rate or the percentage of customers who stop using the app over a certain period.关键绩效指标（KPI）。KPI 衡量特定业务活动的整体成功与表现，让组织洞察战略目标达成得如何。例如，某应用的重要 KPI 可能是流失率，即一段时间内停止使用该应用的客户百分比。
— 原书第 52 页 —

In August 2024, a Gartner Research study predicted that 30% of existing GenAI projects would fail by 2025. (In fact, Gartner published similar findings in 2018, predicting that 85% of ML projects would fail in production by 2022.) The key failure points outlined in the 2024 study are notable because they are the operational aspects of LLM development and deployment—including data quality issues, the lack of a strong evaluation framework, and the high costs of scaling these models in production.

2024 年 8 月，Gartner 研究预测现有 GenAI 项目到 2025 年将有 30% 失败。（事实上 Gartner 在 2018 年也发表过类似结论，预测 85% 的 ML 项目到 2022 年会在生产中失败。）2024 年研究列出的关键失败点值得注意，因为它们都是 LLM 开发和部署的运维方面——包括数据质量问题、缺乏强大的评估框架，以及在生产中扩缩这些模型的高昂成本。

That said, one of the most obvious issues is mismatched expectations between management and engineering teams. For the last 10 years, one of data scientists' biggest skill gaps has been in translating ML model metrics into organizational and product success metrics. In other words, when you're measuring abstract goals like model security, scalability, robustness, and reliability, how do you communicate what this means for the business? That's what SLOs, SLAs, and KPIs are for.

话虽如此，最明显的问题之一是管理层与工程团队之间期望不匹配。过去 10 年，数据科学家最大的技能差距之一，就是把 ML 模型指标翻译成组织和产品成功指标。换句话说，当你衡量模型安全、可扩展、鲁棒、可靠这些抽象目标时，如何把这对业务意味着什么讲清楚？这正是 SLO、SLA、KPI 的用处。

Using an SLO-SLA-KPI framework allows LLMOps teams to automate, streamline, and manage expectations across multiple stakeholders. SLOs make it evident to all stakeholders what level of service is being aimed for. SLAs ensure accountability so that everyone involved is aware of their roles and the agreed-upon service levels. This can also help you track performance and address any deviations from the expected standards. And KPIs provide visibility into real-time data to help detect potential issues early, facilitating informed decision-making.

使用 SLO-SLA-KPI 框架让 LLMOps 团队能跨多个利益相关方自动化、精简并管理期望。SLO 让所有利益相关方清楚目标服务水平；SLA 确保问责，让每位参与者都知道自己的角色和约定的服务水平。这也有助于跟踪表现、处理与预期标准的偏差。KPI 则提供实时数据可见性，帮助及早发现潜在问题，支持有据决策。

The Four Goals of LLMOpsLLMOps 的四大目标

Let's look more closely at the LLMOps goals to see how these metrics translate.

我们更仔细地看看 LLMOps 各目标，看这些指标如何落地。

Reliability. As you know well by now, LLMs are extremely complex, with billions of parameters. Their behavior can be unpredictable, and they sometimes exhibit unexpected responses or errors due to their scale and the intricacies of their training data. Additionally, if the training data is biased, outdated, or unrepresentative of certain domains, the model's performance can be unreliable in those areas.

可靠性。你现在很清楚，LLM 极其复杂，有数十亿参数。它们的行为可能不可预测，由于规模和训练数据的错综，有时会表现出意外的回复或错误。此外，如果训练数据有偏见、过时或不能代表某些领域，模型在那些领域的表现可能不可靠。

LLMs also struggle at times with understanding the context, nuance, and intent behind user queries. This can lead to incorrect, irrelevant, or misleading responses. What's more, LLMs usually aren't updated in real time. As language evolves, if new information is not integrated into the training data via regular retraining, models can become outdated, leading to decreased reliability.

LLM 有时也难以理解用户查询背后的上下文、细微差别和意图。这可能导致错误、不相关或误导性的回复。而且 LLM 通常不是实时更新的。随着语言演变，如果不通过定期再训练把新信息整合进训练数据，模型可能过时，导致可靠性下降。

All of these issues come down to reliability. The reliability of LLM-based applications can be measured in terms of system availability, error rates, and customer satisfaction. Table 2-2 shows how these metrics would look as SLOs, SLAs, and KPIs.

所有这些问题归根到底都是可靠性。基于 LLM 的应用的可靠性可从系统可用性、错误率和客户满意度三方面衡量。表 2-2 展示了这些指标作为 SLO、SLA、KPI 的样子。

Scalability. LLMs tend to have a large memory footprint, often exceeding the capacity of a single machine. Distributing a model across multiple GPUs or nodes while maintaining performance is technically challenging. Handling large volumes of data efficiently is critical.

可扩展性。LLM 往往内存占用很大，常超过单机容量。在多 GPU 或多节点间分布模型同时维持性能，在技术上很有挑战。高效处理海量数据至关重要。

Another significant challenge is scaling the data pipeline to feed data into the model at the required speed without causing bottlenecks. This can be especially hard for applications like chatbots or interactive services, where low latency is crucial. Scaling while keeping response times low can be challenging, since scaling up increases resource contention and network overhead. Therefore, balancing performance with cost efficiency is a constant concern.

另一个重大挑战是扩缩数据流水线，以所需速度把数据喂给模型而不造成瓶颈。对聊天机器人或交互式服务这类低延迟至关重要的应用，这尤其困难。扩缩同时保持低响应时间很有挑战，因为扩大会增加资源争用和网络开销。因此，在性能与成本效率之间平衡是持续的关切。

Robustness. Over time, the statistical properties of the model's training data can change, leading to a drift in the model's performance. This is particularly problematic for models that interact with real-time or rapidly changing data. This can lead to performance degradation in the form of outdated or irrelevant responses.

鲁棒性。随着时间推移，模型训练数据的统计特性可能变化，导致模型性能漂移。对于与实时或快速变化数据交互的模型，这尤其成问题。这可能以过时或不相关回复的形式导致性能退化。

Continuous training and fine-tuning are necessary to maintain robustness, but they require significant computational resources and careful management to avoid introducing new biases or errors. You can measure robustness via metrics like data freshness, model evaluation, and consistency, as shown in Table 2-4.

持续训练和微调对于维持鲁棒性是必要的，但它们需要大量计算资源和谨慎管理，以避免引入新偏见或错误。你可通过数据新鲜度、模型评估和一致性等指标衡量鲁棒性，如表 2-4 所示。

Security. Maintaining LLM application security is challenging: these are complex models handling sensitive data in the face of constantly evolving security threats. LLMs are especially vulnerable to adversarial attacks, data poisoning, and other forms of exploitation that can compromise their integrity and security.

安全性。维护 LLM 应用安全很有挑战：这些是处理敏感数据的复杂模型，面对的是不断演变的安全威胁。LLM 尤其容易受到对抗攻击、数据投毒和其他形式利用的影响，这些可能危及其完整性和安全。

When all teams—whether they are involved in development, operations, or management—understand the agreed-upon service levels and performance indicators, they can work together more effectively toward common goals. This alignment fosters a unified approach to managing and improving project performance. It also helps in making data-backed decisions about resource allocation, process changes, and strategic adjustments. Most importantly, it helps in building trust and ensuring that everyone is on the same page regarding expectations and outcomes.

当所有团队——无论参与开发、运维还是管理——都理解约定的服务水平和绩效指标时，它们就能更有效地朝共同目标协作。这种对齐促进了管理和改进项目绩效的统一方式。它还有助于在资源分配、流程变更和战略调整上做出数据支撑的决策。最重要的是，它有助于建立信任，确保每个人对期望和结果理解一致。

Overall, implementing an SLO-SLA-KPI framework not only enhances transparency and fosters collaboration, but it also serves as a foundational element in evaluating and advancing the maturity of your LLMOps practices, which is the topic of this chapter's final section.

总体而言，实施 SLO-SLA-KPI 框架不仅增强透明度、促进协作，也是评估和推进你 LLMOps 实践成熟度的基础要素——这正是本章最后一节的主题。

The LLMOps Maturity ModelLLMOps 成熟度模型

LLMOps maturity is a way of determining how well an organization's LLM operations align with industry best practices and standards. Assessing LLMOps maturity helps organizations identify their strengths, areas for improvement, and opportunities for scaling and enhancing the robustness of their LLM systems.

LLMOps 成熟度是一种判断组织的 LLM 运维与行业最佳实践和标准对齐程度的方式。评估 LLMOps 成熟度帮助组织识别自身优势、待改进领域，以及扩缩和增强其 LLM 系统鲁棒性的机会。

A few years ago, Microsoft published a machine learning operations maturity model detailing a progressive set of requirements and stages to measure the maturity of MLOps production environments and processes. The LLMOps maturity model we present here, inspired by Microsoft's MLOps model, is meant to do the same for LLMOps teams. Although this is by no means a comprehensive audit, we hope to see several variations put into practice.

几年前，微软发表了一个机器学习运维成熟度模型，详细列出了一套渐进式要求和阶段，用于衡量 MLOps 生产环境和流程的成熟度。我们在此呈现的 LLMOps 成熟度模型受微软 MLOps 模型启发，旨在为 LLMOps 团队做同样的事。虽然这绝非一次全面审计，但我们希望看到若干变体被付诸实践。

— 原书第 56 页 —

The three LLMOps maturity levels are as follows:

LLMOps 成熟度分为三级：

  • Level 0. No LLMOps practices are implemented. The organization's lack of formal structures and processes for managing and deploying its LLM systems hinders its effectiveness.Level 0。未实施任何 LLMOps 实践。组织缺乏管理和部署其 LLM 系统的正式结构和流程，阻碍了效能。
  • Level 1. The organization applies MLOps practices but without LLM-specific adaptations. This is an improvement over Level 0 in terms of formalization and processes but still lacks the sophistication needed for full LLM operations.Level 1。组织应用 MLOps 实践，但没有 LLM 专用的适配。相比 Level 0，在形式化和流程上有所进步，但仍缺少完整 LLM 运维所需的成熟度。
  • Level 2. Achieving Level 2 represents a mature LLMOps state, characterized by advanced documentation, robust monitoring and compliance measures, and the integration of sophisticated orchestration and human review strategies. Usually, this can be assessed by asking some questions about whether decision strategies and model performance measures and metrics are well documented within the team.Level 2。达到 Level 2 代表成熟的 LLMOps 状态，特征是完善的文档、健壮的监控和合规措施，以及复杂编排和人工审查策略的集成。通常可以通过询问团队内部是否对决策策略和模型绩效度量与指标有良好文档化来评估。

Documenting the factors shown in Table 2-6 can be incredibly helpful when choosing and deploying any new model. For example, given the significant costs that are associated with deploying an LLM application, cost-benchmark analysis documentation allows the company to decide which model to roll into production and estimate the project timeline.

在选择和部署任何新模型时，把表 2-6 中的因素文档化非常有帮助。例如，鉴于部署 LLM 应用的巨大成本，成本基准分析文档让公司能决定把哪个模型投产，并估算项目时间线。

After deployment, the company also needs to assess how well the team has documented the model's performance measures and metrics. This is to make sure that everyone on the team understands the expectations and that they are comprehensively monitoring the model performance in production.

部署之后，公司还需要评估团队对模型绩效度量和指标的文档化程度。这是为了确保团队每个人都理解期望，并在生产中全面监控模型性能。

Table 2-7 outlines three levels of LLMOps maturity with regard to model performance and evaluation. Keeping these different levels in mind, organizations and the LLMOps team will be better prepared to deal with contingencies and can better align projects with business goals, mitigate risks, and enhance operational efficiency.

表 2-7 概述了在模型性能和评估方面 LLMOps 成熟度的三个层级。牢记这些不同层级，组织和 LLMOps 团队将更好地应对突发情况，并能更好地让项目与业务目标对齐、缓解风险、提升运营效率。

LLM 的输入输出是否自动存储？无自动存储基础的输入输出存储自动存储所有输入输出并建索引，便于检索分析
是否定期做 A/B 测试？无 A/B 测试偶尔 A/B 测试，覆盖有限定期 A/B 测试，覆盖全面并用 Optimizely 或自定义框架分析

Let's look at these levels in more detail:

我们更详细地看看这些层级：

  • Level 0: No LLMOps. Machine learning efforts are often isolated and experimental, and they lack any systematic deployment and monitoring framework. The models may be developed in silos, often resulting in unreliability and inefficiency. Chevrolet's chatbot blunder is an excellent example; due to a lack of monitoring and guardrails, the app was abused by the community for algebra homework. It also offered Chevrolet cars in no-take-backsies deals and promoted Tesla cars instead.Level 0：无 LLMOps。机器学习工作常是孤立和实验性的，缺乏系统的部署和监控框架。模型可能在孤岛中开发，往往导致不可靠和低效。雪佛兰聊天机器人翻车就是绝佳例子；由于缺乏监控和护栏，该应用被社区用来写代数作业，还以“不许反悔”的条件推销雪佛兰汽车，反而推广起了特斯拉。
  • Level 1: MLOps, no LLMOps. The organization is likely to have a robust pipeline for model training, testing, and deployment, with automated monitoring and retraining workflows. However, this setup is designed to build for small models and is not fully optimized for the specific challenges of LLMs.Level 1：MLOps，无 LLMOps。组织很可能有健壮的模型训练、测试和部署流水线，以及自动化监控和再训练工作流。但这套设置是为小模型构建的，并未针对 LLM 的特定挑战做充分优化。
  • Level 2: Full LLMOps. At the highest level of maturity, the organization has adopted LLMOps practices and is fully optimized for LLM applications. Its infrastructure is capable of handling large-scale LLM deployments, fine-tuning, real-time inference, auto-scaling, and resource management. Mature LLMOps teams have failover and rollback mechanisms in place and can act quickly if the updated model underperforms after deployment. The organization can deliver more reliable responses, get a good ROI, and reduce operational risks.Level 2：完整 LLMOps。在最高成熟度层级，组织已采用 LLMOps 实践并为 LLM 应用充分优化。其基础设施能处理大规模 LLM 部署、微调、实时推理、自动扩缩和资源管理。成熟的 LLMOps 团队有故障转移和回滚机制，如果更新后的模型部署后表现不佳，能迅速应对。组织能交付更可靠的回复、获得良好 ROI，并降低运营风险。

Conclusion小结

In this chapter, we discussed the team structure for organizations building LLM applications. We discussed various roles and how to build a highly effective team. Finally, we discussed a framework for typing the LLM performance metrics with the business KPIs. In the next chapter, we will talk about how LLMs have changed the data engineering landscape, and we'll show you how to build performant data pipelines for LLMs.

本章讨论了构建 LLM 应用的组织的团队结构，讨论了各种角色以及如何构建高效团队。最后讨论了把 LLM 性能指标与业务 KPI 关联起来的框架。下一章我们将讨论 LLM 如何改变了数据工程格局，并展示如何为 LLM 构建高性能数据流水线。
